title: Canonical project tracker and architecture issue synchronization

C1.rule: Mechanical, one owned file, fully specified, no design choice

C2.rule: Bounded implementation or tests, clear spec, one or two owned files and their tests

C3.rule: Cross-module design; changes a gate or the ledger contract; wrong means every project inherits it

C4.rule: Planning, merging, reconciling, anything in a project's real data, a sponsor decision

asks.quote:
Update Common Rules to support a single canonical project tracker with
architecture-group GitHub issue synchronization.

Project: EisKaffee Vanilla
Workspace ID: eiskaffee-vanilla
Hub repository: docs
Issue repository: EisKaffee-ai/bean-engine
Issue mutations must use the integrated GitHub plugin, not github.com UI.

CURRENT STATE

- The Docs delivery catalogue contains:
  - 27 architecture/feature groups
  - 59 features
  - 362 lifecycle items
- The 27 group ledgers already exist under:
  content/proposal/delivery/docs/proposals/
- Every feature normally has these lifecycle stages:
  D — architecture and workflow
  R — owner approval
  A — code alignment
  I — missing implementation
  U — UI/consumer integration
  V — verification and evidence
- The generated website tracker already renders these 27 proposals.
- docs/architecture/vanilla-traceability.json is a generated traceability
  dataset. It is not an independent tracker.
- Bean Engine is the single GitHub issue home for this workspace.

REQUIRED OUTCOME

There must be exactly one published tracker for the Docs project.

Canonical ledger directory:
content/proposal/delivery/docs/proposals

Canonical tracker:
content/proposal/delivery/docs/proposals/tracker/index.html

The IceKaffee.ai website must publish this generated tracker from a committed
Docs revision. It must not maintain a manually edited or separately generated
copy.

The joined repository status for Vanilla, Bean Engine, Docs and UI Assets must
appear as a section of this tracker rather than as a second public tracker.
Intermediate generated files may remain internal build artifacts.

GITHUB ISSUE MODEL

Create exactly one GitHub issue for each of the 27 architecture groups.

Issue granularity: one issue per proposal/group, not one issue per feature and
not one issue per lifecycle row.

Issue title format:

[Architecture 08/27] Engine · Media access & rendition

Each issue body must be generated from its owning ledger and contain:

1. Architecture group ID, namespace and layer.
2. Link to the canonical tracker and architecture source.
3. Workflow/source revision.
4. Repository ownership:
   - Docs — architecture and requirements
   - Vanilla — application, SDK and UI
   - Bean Engine — business logic and Runner
   - UI Assets — shared visual assets
5. One checklist entry for every ledger item, preserving its item ID.
6. Current evidence, gaps, dependencies and next action.
7. Links to implementation files, tests, receipts and related issues.

Example checklist:

## engine.media.preview

- [x] D-01 — Architecture and workflow
- [x] R-01 — Owner approval
- [x] A-01 — Code alignment
- [ ] I-01 — Missing implementation · in progress
- [ ] U-01 — UI integration
- [ ] V-01 — Feature completion and evidence

For groups containing multiple features, repeat the six-stage checklist under
each feature heading. Therefore a group with two features has 12 checkboxes.

For groups whose detailed features are not defined yet, create the issue with
the existing scope-definition ledger item. Do not invent requirements merely
to fill the issue.

ONE-WAY SYNCHRONIZATION

The ledger is authoritative.

- Ledger status `done` becomes a checked GitHub checkbox.
- `deferred` becomes checked only when its reason is included.
- All other statuses remain unchecked and display their explicit state.
- Every ledger item in a group links to the same group issue.
- Ledger updates regenerate the issue body through the integrated GitHub
  plugin.
- Manual checkbox edits on GitHub must never silently update the ledger.
  They require an explicit Common Rules reconciliation with evidence.
- Close an issue only when all its rows are terminal and completion evidence
  is attached.
- Reopen it if an authoritative ledger row is reopened.

Add support for these optional project settings:

integration.issue_linking = "one-way"
integration.issue_repository = "EisKaffee-ai/bean-engine"
integration.issue_granularity = "proposal"
integration.issue_sync_direction = "ledger-to-github"

Do not implement two-way synchronization.

TRACKER INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE

Keep one page with these main views:

- Overview
- Product delivery
- Architecture
- Repositories
- Evidence

Inside Architecture, group the 27 issues by layer:

- Application: proposals 1, 2, 26, 27
- Runner: proposals 3–5
- Engine: proposals 6, 8–11, 14, 15
- Memory: proposals 7, 12, 13, 20–25
- AI: proposals 16–19

Each architecture card must show:

- proposal/group number and title;
- linked GitHub issue;
- feature count;
- completed/total checklist rows;
- architecture approval status;
- implementation classification;
- repository owners;
- blockers and next action.

The 59-feature traceability matrix should be accessible as a drill-down from
these cards, not published as another tracker.

MIGRATION REQUIREMENTS

- Preserve all 27 ledger IDs, 362 lifecycle item IDs, history and evidence.
- Do not copy member ledgers into Docs.
- Import any existing Docs tracker coordination rows into the canonical page
  as Project Operations rather than maintaining another published tracker.
- Preserve Bean Engine issue #2 as the issue for Proposal 08 rather than
  creating a duplicate.
- Generate drafts for the other 26 issues and validate them before creating
  them.
- Use the integrated GitHub plugin for issue creation and updates.
- Never infer “implemented” from a source-path mention.
- Only revision-bound tests and receipts may complete verification rows.

COMMON RULES ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. Setup preview identifies the existing 27 ledgers and proposes no duplicate
   tracker.
2. The Docs manifest points to the canonical ledger directory.
3. Issue linking is one-way and names the Bean Engine issue repository.
4. Exactly 27 architecture group issues exist.
5. Every lifecycle row maps to exactly one group issue.
6. Every issue checkbox maps back to a stable ledger item ID.
7. Tracker totals equal ledger totals and issue checkbox totals.
8. The website tracker is generated from the committed canonical ledgers.
9. No second public tracker exists for the project.
10. Doctor, tracecheck, tracker validation, workspace validation and the Docs
    build all pass.
asks.note: Accepted scope: implement in Common Rules and release a new plugin version.

asks.quote: Make a goal, implement the common rules and release a new version of the plugin.

Also before creating the next release, please optimize, like when this plugin is loaded, how much memory it utilizes in the context. I want those analysis, and that analysis should also be part of the readme.
asks.note: Release 1.10.0 must include measured context-loading analysis, optimization and README documentation before publication.

asks.quote: And optimize the test run time. Move fast.
asks.note: Release 1.10.0 must reduce full-gate wall time without reducing coverage and publish timing evidence.

asks.quote: When can we have the common rules released?
asks.note: Release timing depends on clearing the final Common Rules gate, independent review, and downstream read-only acceptance evidence.

asks.quote: What is the blocking point? Remove the user-owned files. I don't want to keep any legacy files if they are no longer required, and proceed ahead with the implementation, remove all the blocks.
asks.note: Remove local-only user edits, retain files proven load-bearing, delete only genuinely obsolete compatibility copies, and continue through release gates.

asks.quote: And then why is it taking so time? You're not creating a feature. You're just creating this common rule infrastructure. And please make sure that the tracker and all the elements are being managed through Python and not through AI, because I see a lot of problems with the current tracker. So anything that can use tracking should be done through Python scripts, which is repeatable and not through AI.
asks.note: Treat the work as deterministic Common Rules infrastructure: Python owns tracker state transitions, validation, issue plans, write-back, rendering and freshness checks; agents only supply explicit inputs and invoke the tools.

asks.quote: Number or anything that's being generated anywhere, that should be through scripts always. And that is part of the plugin that we are shipping. It should not be done through AI regardless.
asks.note: All generated identifiers, counts, digests, plans, mappings, summaries, checkpoints and rendered artifacts must be produced or recorded by scripts shipped in the plugin; AI never fabricates or directly writes generated values.
